  76+ 0000 ~                                    ldCopy2Byte vectorX, varR           ; Set (S R) = nosev_x

  78+ 0000 ~                                    call madXAequQmulAaddRS             ; Set (A X) = Q * A + (S R)

  35+ 0000              ;-- Name: LL28 Calculate R = 256 * A / Q
  36+ 0000              ;-- LL28+4              Skips the A >= Q check and always returns with C flag cleared, so this can be called if we know the division will work
  37+ 0000              ;-- LL31                Skips the A >= Q check and does not set the R counter, so this can be used for jumping straight into the division loop if R is already set to 254 and we know the division will work
  38+ 0000              ;   Reg mapping 6502  Z80
  39+ 0000              ;               a     a
  40+ 0000              ;               b     x
  41+ 0000              ;               c     q

  45+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL28_6502:         ld      hl,Qvar                 ; CMP Q                  \ If A >= Q, then the answer will not fit in one byte,
  46+ 0000 ~                                        ld      c,(hl)                  ; using c as Q var
  47+ 0000 ~                                        cp      c
  48+ 0000 ~                                        FlipCarryFlag
  49+ 0000 ~                                        jp      c, prefix1?_LL2_6502    ; BCS LL2                \ so jump to LL2 to return 255
  50+ 0000 ~                                        ld      b,$FE                   ; LDX #%11111110         \ Set R to have bits 1-7 set, so we can rotate through 7 loop iterations, getting a 1 each time, and then we use b as Rvar

  52+ 0000 ~                                        jp      c, prefix1?_LL29_6502             ; BCS LL29               \ If bit 7 of A was set, then jump straight to the subtraction
  53+ 0000 ~                                        FlipCarryFlag                   ;                          If A < N, then C flag is set.
  54+ 0000 ~                                        JumpIfALTNusng c, prefix1?_LL31_SKIPSUB_6502 ; CMP Q              \ If A < Q, skip the following subtraction
  55+ 0000 ~                                                                            ; BCC P%+4
  56+ 0000 ~                                        sub     c                       ; SBC Q                  \ A >= Q, so set A = A - Q
  57+ 0000 ~                                        ClearCarryFlag
  58+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL31_SKIPSUB_6502:  FlipCarryFlag
  59+ 0000 ~                                        rl      b                       ; ROL R                  \ Rotate the counter in R to the left, and catch the result bit into bit 0 (which will be a 0 if we didn't do the subtraction, or 1 if we did)
  60+ 0000 ~                                        jp      c, prefix1?_LL31_6502            ; BCS LL31               \ If we still have set bits in R, loop back to LL31 to do the next iteration of 7
  61+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,b

  64+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL29_6502:          sub     c                       ; SBC Q                  \ A >= Q, so set A = A - Q

  66+ 0000 ~                                        rl      b                       ; ROL R                  \ Rotate the counter in R to the left, and catch the result bit into bit 0 (which will be a 0 if we didn't do the subtraction, or 1 if we did)

 145+ 0000              ; In XX1510 x1 as a 16-bit coordinate (x1_hi x1_lo)
 146+ 0000              ;    XX1532 y1 as a 16-bit coordinate (y1_hi y1_lo)
 147+ 0000              ;    XX12p2 The line's gradient * 256 (so 1.0 = 256)
 148+ 0000              ;    XX12p3 The direction of slope: * Positive = top left to bottom right * Negative (bit 7 set) = top right to bottom left
 149+ 0000              ;    T      The gradient of slope:* 0 if it's a shallow slope * &FF if it's a steep slope
 150+ 0000              ;  Out  XX150               x1 as an 8-bit coordinate

 155+ 0000              ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 157+ 0000              ;--   * If T = 0, this is a shallow slope, so calculate (Y X) = (S x1_lo) * XX12+2
 158+ 0000              ;--   * If T <> 0, this is a steep slope, so calculate (Y X) = (S x1_lo) / XX12+2

 530+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL138_6502:          call    prefix1?_LL118_6502              ; JSR LL118              \ Call LL118 to move (x1, y1) along the line onto the screen, i.e. clip the line at the (x1, y1) end
 531+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,( prefix1?_XX13)                ; LDA XX13               \ If XX13 = 0, i.e. (x2, y2) is on-screen, jump down to
 532+ 0000 ~                                        and     a
 533+ 0000 ~                                        jp      p,prefix1?_LL124_6502            ; BPL LL124              \ LL124 to return with a successfully clipped line
 534+ 0000 ~            ;-- If we get here, XX13 = 191 (128) (both coordinates areoff-screen)
 535+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL117_6502:          ld      a,(prefix1?_XX1510+1)            ; LDA XX15+1             \ If either of x1_hi or y1_hi are non-zero, jump to
 536+ 0000 ~                                        ld      hl,prefix1?_XX1532+1             ; ORA XX15+3             \ LL137 to return from the subroutine with the C flag
 537+ 0000 ~                                        or      (hl)
 538+ 0000 ~                                        jp      nz, prefix1?_LL137_6502          ; BNE LL137              \ set, as the line doesn't fit on-screen
 539+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,(prefix1?_XX1532)              ; LDA XX15+2             \ If y1_lo > y-coordinate of the bottom of the screen
 540+ 0000 ~                                        cp      128                     ; CMP #Y*2               \ jump to LL137 to return from the subroutine with the
 541+ 0000 ~                                        jp      nc, prefix1?_LL137_6502          ; BCS LL137              \ C flag set, as the line doesn't fit on-screen
 542+ 0000 ~            ;-- If we get here, XX13 = 95 or 191, and in both cases (x2, y2) is off-screen, so we now need to swap the (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) coordinates around before doing the actual clipping, because we need to clip (x2, y2) but the clipping routine at LL118 only clips (x1, y1)
 543+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LLX117_6502:         ld      hl,( prefix1?_XX1510)             ; LDX XX15               \ Swap x1_lo = x2_lo
 544+ 0000 ~                                        ld      de,( prefix1?_XX1554)
 545+ 0000 ~                                        ld      ( prefix1?_XX1510),de
 546+ 0000 ~                                        ld      ( prefix1?_XX1554),hl
 547+ 0000 ~                                        ld      hl,( prefix1?_XX1532)             ; LDX XX15+2             \ Swap y1_lo = y2_lo
 548+ 0000 ~                                        ld      de,( prefix1?_XX1576)
 549+ 0000 ~                                        ld      ( prefix1?_XX1532),de
 550+ 0000 ~                                        ld      ( prefix1?_XX1576),hl
 551+ 0000 ~                                        call    prefix1?_LL118_6502              ; JSR LL118              \ Call LL118 to move (x1, y1) along the line onto the screen, i.e. clip the line at the (x1, y1) end
 552+ 0000 ~                                        ld      hl,SWAP
 553+ 0000 ~                                        dec     (hl)                    ; DEC SWAP               \ Set SWAP = &FF to indicate that we just clipped the line at the (x2, y2) end by swapping the coordinates (the DEC does this as we set SWAP to 0 at the start of this subroutine)
 554+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL124_6502:          pop     af                      ; PLA            SP+0    \ Restore Y from the stack so it gets preserved through
 555+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Yreg),a                ; TAY                    \ the call to this subroutine
 556+ 0000 ~                                        call    prefix1?_LL146_6502              ; JMP LL146              \ Jump up to LL146 to move the low bytes of (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) into (X1, Y1) and (X2, Y2), and return from the subroutine with a successfully clipped line
 557+ 0000 ~                                        ret                             ; then exit so we don't pop it twice
 558+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL137_6502:          pop     af                      ; PLA            SP+0    \ Restore Y from the stack so it gets preserved through
 559+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Yreg),a                ; TAY                    \ the call to this subroutine
 560+ 0000 ~                                        SetCarryFlag                    ; SEC                    \ Set the C flag to indicate the clipped line does not fit on-screen
 561+ 0000 ~                                        ret                             ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine
 562+ 0000 ~
 563+ 0000 ~
 564+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_l2_draw_6502_line:   ld      hl,x1                           ; copy from currnet position to 6502 variables
 565+ 0000 ~                                        ld      de, prefix1?_XX1510
 566+ 0000 ~                                        ld      bc,4*2
 567+ 0000 ~                                        ldir
 568+ 0000 ~                                        call    prefix1?_LL145_6502                      ; perform 6502 version
 569+ 0000 ~                                        ret     c                               ; returns if carry is set as its a no draw
 570+ 0000 ~            .CopyBackResults:           ld      hl,0
 571+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (x1),hl
 572+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (y1),hl
 573+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (x2),hl
 574+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (y2),hl
 575+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,( prefix1?_XX1510)
 576+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (x1),a
 577+ 0000 ~                                        ld      c,a

  89+ 0000              ; Sets IYH to sign bits, bit 7 = x, bit 6 = y bit 5 = z
  90+ 0000              SetIYHToSignBits:       MACRO
  91+ 0000 ~                                    ld      a,(ix+POS_ZSGNOFFSET)   ; get Z sign
  92+ 0000 ~                                    and     $80                     ; and shift it via A into IYH bit 7
  93+ 0000 ~                                    srl     a                       ;
  94+ 0000 ~                                    ld      iyh,a                   ;
  95+ 0000 ~                                    ld      a,(ix+POS_YSGNOFFSET)   ; get Y sign
  96+ 0000 ~                                    and     $80                     ; and shift it via A into IYH bit 7
  97+ 0000 ~                                    or      iyh                     ; which moves Z into IYH bit 6
  98+ 0000 ~                                    srl     a                       ;
  99+ 0000 ~                                    ld      iyh,a                   ;
 100+ 0000 ~                                    ld      a,(ix+POS_XSGNOFFSET)   ; get X sign
 101+ 0000 ~                                    and     $80                     ; and shift it via A into IYH bit 7
 102+ 0000 ~                                    or      iyh                     ; which moves Y into IYH bit 6 and Z into IYH bit 5
 103+ 0000 ~                                    ld      iyh,a                   ;
 104+ 0000                                      ENDM

 743  937C                  INCLUDE "./Maths/asm_arctan.asm"
# file opened: asm_arctan.asm
   1+ 937C              ;Calculate A = arctan(P / Q)
   2+ 937C              ; This finds the angle in the right-angled triangle where the opposite side to angle A is length P and the adjacent side to angle A has
   3+ 937C              ; length Q, so:  tan(A) = P / Q
   4+ 937C              ;
   5+ 937C              ; The result in A is an integer representing the angle in radians. The routine returns values in the range 0 to 128,  (or 0 to PI radians).
   6+ 937C 3A E1 7E     ARCTAN:                 ld      a,(varP)                    ; LDA P                  \ Set T1 = P EOR Q, which will have the sign of P * Q
   7+ 937F 21 EF 7F                             ld      hl,varQ                     ; EOR Q
   8+ 9382 AE                                   xor     (hl)                        ; .
   9+ 9383 32 DE 7E                             ld      (varT1),a                   ; STA T1
  10+ 9386 3A EF 7F                             ld      a,(varQ)                    ; LDA Q                  \ If Q = 0, jump to AR2 to return a right angle
  11+ 9389 A7                                   and     a                           ; BEQ AR2
  12+ 938A CA CC 93                             jp      z, .AR2                     ; .
  13+ 938D CB 27                                sla     a                           ; ASL A                  \ Set Q = |Q| * 2 (this is a quick way of clearing the
  14+ 938F 32 EF 7F                             ld      (varQ),a                    ; STA Q                  \ sign bit, and we don't need to shift right again as we only ever use this value in the division with |P| * 2, which we set next)
  15+ 9392 3A E1 7E                             ld      a,(varP)                    ; LDA P                  \ Set A = |P| * 2
  16+ 9395 CB 27                                sla     a                           ; ASL A
  17+ 9397 32 E1 7E                             ld      (varP),a
  18+ 939A 21 EF 7F                             ld      hl,varQ
  19+ 939D BE                                   cp      (hl)                        ; CMP Q                  \ If A >= Q, i.e. |P| > |Q|, jump to AR1 to swap P
  20+ 939E D2 B0 93                             jp      nc, .AR1                    ; BCS AR1                \ and Q around, so we can still use the lookup table
  21+ 93A1 CD D8 93                             call    ARS1                        ; JSR ARS1               \ Call ARS1 to set the following from the lookup table:  A = arctan(A / Q)  = arctan(|P / Q|)
  22+ 93A4                                      ClearCarryFlag                      ; SEC                    \ Set the C flag so the SBC instruction in AR3 will be correct, should we jump there
  22+ 93A4 B7          >                        or a
  23+ 93A5 4F           .AR4:                   ld      c,a                         ; as we have to use a we use c as a temp, we can't push af as we would loose flags on pop
  24+ 93A6 3A DE 7E                             ld      a,(varT1)                   ; LDX T1                 \ If T1 is negative, i.e. P and Q have different signs,
  25+ 93A9 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; .
  26+ 93AA A7                                   and     a                           ; BMI AR3                \ jump down to AR3 to return arctan(-|P / Q|)
  27+ 93AB 79                                   ld      a,c                         ; .                      \ we need to get a back before jump
  28+ 93AC FA CF 93                             jp      m, .AR3                     ; .
  29+ 93AF C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Otherwise P and Q have the same sign, so our result is correct and we can return from the subroutine
  30+ 93B0              ; We want to calculate arctan(t) where |t| > 1, so we can use the calculation described in the documentation for the ACT table, i.e. 64 - arctan(1 / t)
  31+ 93B0              ; In the 6502 verion it works with A already being P but we will fetch it
  32+ 93B0 3A EF 7F     .AR1:                   ld      a,(varQ)                    ; LDX Q                  \ Swap the values in Q and P, using the fact that we
  33+ 93B3 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; .
  34+ 93B4 3A E1 7E                             ld      a,(varP)                    ; STA Q                  \ called AR1 with A = P
  35+ 93B7 32 EF 7F                             ld      (varQ),a                    ; .
  36+ 93BA 78                                   ld      a,b                         ; TXA                    \ This also sets A = P (which now contains the original argument |Q|)
  37+ 93BB 32 E1 7E                             ld      (varP),a                    ; STX P                  \
  38+ 93BE CD D8 93                             call    ARS1                        ; JSR ARS1               \ Call ARS1 to set the following from the lookup table: A = arctan(A / Q) = arctan(|Q / P|) = arctan(1 / |P / Q|)
  39+ 93C1 32 0B 80                             ld      (varT),a                    ; STA T                  \ Set T = 64 - T, we use B as T (its not really that)
  40+ 93C4 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; its actually t = a, a = 64-a
  41+ 93C5 3E 40                                ld      a,64                        ; LDA #64 What is going on here is t = result
  42+ 93C7                                      ClearCarryFlag                      ; SBC T                            a = 64- result
  42+ 93C7 B7          >                        or a
  43+ 93C8 98                                   sbc     a,b                         ; .
  44+ 93C9 C3 A5 93                             jp      .AR4                        ; BCS AR4                \ Jump to AR4 to continue the calculation (this BCS is effectively a JMP as the subtraction will never underflow, as ARS1 returns values in the range 0-31)
  45+ 93CC              ; If we get here then Q = 0, so tan(A) = infinity and A is a right angle, or 0.25 of a circle. We allocate 255 to a full circle, so we should return 63 for a right angle
  46+ 93CC 3E 3F        .AR2:                   ld      a,63                        ; LDA #63                \ Set A to 63, to represent a right angle
  47+ 93CE C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine
  48+ 93CF              ; A contains arctan(|P / Q|) but P and Q have different signs, so we need to return arctan(-|P / Q|), using the calculation described in the documentation for the ACT table, i.e. 128 - A
  49+ 93CF 32 0B 80     .AR3:                   ld      (varT),a
  50+ 93D2 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; STA T                  \ Set A = 128 - A, we use b as T
  51+ 93D3 3E 80                                ld      a,128                       ; LDA #128               \
  52+ 93D5                                      ClearCarryFlag                      ; SBC T                  \ The subtraction will work because we did a SEC before calling AR3
  52+ 93D5 B7          >                        or a
  53+ 93D6 98                                   sbc     a,b
  54+ 93D7 C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine
  55+ 93D8              ; This routine fetches arctan(A / Q) from the ACT table, so A will be set to an integer in the range 0 to 31 that represents an angle from 0 to 45 degrees (or 0 to \ PI / 4 radians)
  56+ 93D8              ARS1:                   MMUSelectMathsTables
  56+ 93D8 ED 91 50 63 >                     nextreg MathsTablesMMU,    BankMathsTables
  57+ 93DC CD 7F 08                             call    Amul256DivQ                 ; JSR LL28               \ Call LL28 to calculate: R = 256 * A / Q
  58+ 93DF 3A F0 7F                             ld      a,(varR)                    ; LDA R                  \ Set X = R / 8
  59+ 93E2 CB 3F                                srl     a                           ; LSR A                  \       = 32 * A / Q
  60+ 93E4 CB 3F                                srl     a                           ; LSR A                  \
  61+ 93E6 CB 3F                                srl     a                           ; LSR A                  \ so X has the value t * 32 where t = A / Q, which is
  62+ 93E8 21 0F 94                             ld      hl,ACT                      ; TAX                    \ what we need to look up values in the ACT table
  63+ 93EB ED 31                                add     hl,a                        ; LDA ACT,X              \ Fetch ACT+X from the ACT table into A, so now:
  64+ 93ED 7E                                   ld      a,(hl)                      ;                        \   A = value in ACT + X = value in ACT + (32 * A / Q)= arctan(A / Q)
  65+ 93EE C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine
  66+ 93EF
  67+ 93EF              ;;;arctan:										; .ARCTAN	\ -> &2A3C  \ A=TAN-1(P/Q) \ A=arctan (P/Q)  called from block E

   3+ 95FE              ; Calculate the following between sign-magnitude numbers:
   4+ 95FE              ;   (S A) = (S R) + (A Q)
   5+ 95FE              ; where the sign bytes only contain the sign bits, not magnitudes.
   6+ 95FE              ; note goes wrong at <-127 >128 so need 16 bit version

  10+ 95FE              ;	ld		a,(varQ)
  11+ 95FE              ;	ld		e,a

  14+ 95FE              ;	ld		a,(varR)
  15+ 95FE              ;	ld		l,a

  18+ 95FE              ;	ld		(varS),a
  19+ 95FE              ;	ld		a,l

  22+ 95FE              ;   R     Q    Op            Sign calc
  23+ 95FE              ;	10    5    Add           +    sign same add R sign
  24+ 95FE              ;   -10   5    ABS Sub       -    sign diff ABS R > S sub R sign
  25+ 95FE              ;   10   -5    ABS sub       +    sign diff ABS R > S sub R sign
  26+ 95FE              ;	-10  -5    ABS Add       -    sign same add R sign

  29+ 95FE              ;   5    -10   swap ABS Sub  -    sign diff ABS Q > R swap SUB R sign

 528+ C473              ; 12   X1            X2    OK         2 LT X1
 529+ C473              ; 1    X1  2         X2    FAIL       1 LT X1 && 2 GT X1 && 2 LT X2

 532+ C473              ;      X1            X2 12 OK         1 GT X2

 534+ C473              ; Carry flag is set on failure
 535+ C473              ;                 cache left   between
 536+ C473
 537+ C473              ;   h =top row, l = bottom row <not needed now>, d = left, e = right, ix = pointer to data
 538+ C473              ;   If A == N, then Z flag is set.
 539+ C473              ;   If A != N, then Z flag is reset.
 540+ C473              ;   If A < N, then C flag is set.

 206+ EFFD E5           .IsTotallyOffLeft:  push    hl                              ; if X pos + length <0 then no line

 212+ F005 E1                               pop     hl                              ; .
 213+ F006 F8                               ret     m                               ; if x + distance < 0 then off screen skip
 214+ F007              ;-- now as its on screen but clipped x < 0 we can just draw a line from 0 to x+d, maxed at x+d = 255

 273+ F13D
 274+ F13D              ;-- Name: LL28 Calculate R = 256 * A / Q
 275+ F13D              ;-- LL28+4              Skips the A >= Q check and always returns with C flag cleared, so this can be called if we know the division will work
 276+ F13D              ;-- LL31                Skips the A >= Q check and does not set the R counter, so this can be used for jumping straight into the division loop if R is already set to 254 and we know the division will work
 277+ F13D              ;   Reg mapping 6502  Z80
 278+ F13D              ;               a     a
 279+ F13D              ;               b     x
 280+ F13D              ;               c     q
 281+ F13D              ;               d     r
 282+ F13D              ;
 283+ F13D 21 38 F1     LL28_6502:          ld      hl,Qvar                 ; CMP Q                  \ If A >= Q, then the answer will not fit in one byte,
 284+ F140 4E                               ld      c,(hl)                  ; using c as Q var
 285+ F141 B9                               cp      c
 286+ F142                                  FlipCarryFlag
 286+ F142 3F          >                        ccf
 287+ F143 DA 6B F1                         jp      c, LL2_6502             ; BCS LL2                \ so jump to LL2 to return 255
 288+ F146 06 FE                            ld      b,$FE                   ; LDX #%11111110         \ Set R to have bits 1-7 set, so we can rotate through 7 loop iterations, getting a 1 each time, and then we use b as Rvar
 289+ F148 CB 27        LL31_6502:          sla     a                       ; ASL A                  \ Shift A to the left
 290+ F14A DA 5F F1                         jp      c,LL29_6502             ; BCS LL29               \ If bit 7 of A was set, then jump straight to the subtraction
 291+ F14D                                  FlipCarryFlag                   ;                          If A < N, then C flag is set.
 291+ F14D 3F          >                        ccf
 292+ F14E                                  JumpIfALTNusng c, LL31_SKIPSUB_6502 ; CMP Q              \ If A < Q, skip the following subtraction
 292+ F14E B9          >                        cp      c
 292+ F14F DA 54 F1    >                        jp		c, LL31_SKIPSUB_6502
 293+ F152                                                                  ; BCC P%+4
 294+ F152 91                               sub     c                       ; SBC Q                  \ A >= Q, so set A = A - Q
 295+ F153                                  ClearCarryFlag
 295+ F153 B7          >                        or a
 296+ F154              LL31_SKIPSUB_6502:  FlipCarryFlag
 296+ F154 3F          >                        ccf
 297+ F155 CB 10                            rl      b                       ; ROL R                  \ Rotate the counter in R to the left, and catch the result bit into bit 0 (which will be a 0 if we didn't do the subtraction, or 1 if we did)
 298+ F157 DA 48 F1                         jp      c, LL31_6502            ; BCS LL31               \ If we still have set bits in R, loop back to LL31 to do the next iteration of 7
 299+ F15A 78                               ld      a,b
 300+ F15B 32 39 F1                         ld      (Rvar),a
 301+ F15E C9                               ret                             ; RTS                    \ R left with remainder of division
 302+ F15F 91           LL29_6502:          sub     c                       ; SBC Q                  \ A >= Q, so set A = A - Q
 303+ F160                                  SetCarryFlag                    ; SEC                    \ Set the C flag to rotate into the result in R
 303+ F160 37          >                        scf
 304+ F161 CB 10                            rl      b                       ; ROL R                  \ Rotate the counter in R to the left, and catch the result bit into bit 0 (which will be a 0 if we didn't do the subtraction, or 1 if we did)
 305+ F163 DA 48 F1                         jp      c, LL31_6502            ; BCS LL31               \ If we still have set bits in R, loop back to LL31 to do the next iteration of 7
 306+ F166 78                               ld      a,b                     ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine with R containing the
 307+ F167 32 39 F1                         ld      (Rvar),a                ; .
 308+ F16A C9                               ret                             ; .                      \ remainder of the division
 309+ F16B 3E FF        LL2_6502:           ld      a,$FF                   ; LDA #255               \ The division is very close to 1, so return the closest
 310+ F16D 32 39 F1                         ld      (Rvar),a                ; STA R                  \ possible answer to 256, i.e. R = 255
 311+ F170                                  SetCarryFlag                    ; we failed so need carry flag set
 311+ F170 37          >                        scf
 312+ F171 C9                               ret                             ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine

# file opened: l2_draw_line_v2.asm
   1+ FE9C              ; ******************************************************************************
   2+ FE9C              ;
   3+ FE9C              ;	Draw a pixel line from (x0,y0) defined in (COORDS) - the current plot
   4+ FE9C              ;	coordinate, to the relative distance points (x0+x,y0+y).
   5+ FE9C              ;
   6+ FE9C              ;	Design & programming by Gunther Strube,	Copyright (C) InterLogic 1995
   7+ FE9C              ;
   8+ FE9C              ;	The (COORDS+0)	pointer contains the current y coordinate, (COORDS+1) the
   9+ FE9C              ;	current x coordinate. The main program should reset the (COORDS) variables
  10+ FE9C              ;	before using line drawing.
  11+ FE9C              ;
  12+ FE9C              ;	The routine checks the range of specified coordinates which is the
  13+ FE9C              ;	boundaries of the graphics area (256x64	pixels).
  14+ FE9C              ;	If a boundary error occurs the routine exits automatically.	This may be
  15+ FE9C              ;	useful if you are trying to draw a line longer than allowed. Only the
  16+ FE9C              ;	visible part will be drawn.
  17+ FE9C              ;
  18+ FE9C              ;	The hardware graphics memory is organized as (0,0) in the top left corner.
  19+ FE9C              ;
  20+ FE9C              ;	The plot routine is	defined by an address pointer	in IX.
  21+ FE9C              ;
  22+ FE9C              ;	IN:	HL =	move	relative x horisontal points (maximum +/- 255).
  23+ FE9C              ;		DE =	move	relative y vertical	points (maximum +/-	255).
  24+ FE9C              ;		IX =	pointer to plot routine that uses HL = (x,y)	of plot coordinate.
  25+ FE9C              ;
  26+ FE9C              ;	OUT:	None.
  27+ FE9C              ;
  28+ FE9C              ;	Registers	used	by routine:
  29+ FE9C              ;		   N	:	B, loop counter
  30+ FE9C              ;		   i	:	line	balance variable
  31+ FE9C              ;		   x	:	H/L,	horisontal, vertical distance	variables
  32+ FE9C              ;		   y	:	H/L,	horisontal, vertical distance	variables
  33+ FE9C              ;	  (x0,y0)	:	(h,l)
  34+ FE9C              ;	  direc_x	:	d, horisontal step increment
  35+ FE9C              ;	  direc_y	:	e, vertical step increment
  36+ FE9C              ;		 ddx	:	b, horisontal step increment
  37+ FE9C              ;		 ddy	:	c, vertical step increment
  38+ FE9C              ;
  39+ FE9C              ;		DE, A work registers.
  40+ FE9C              ;
  41+ FE9C              ; The algorithm in pseudo-code:
  42+ FE9C              ;
  43+ FE9C              ;	direc_x =	SGN x: direc_y	= SGN y
  44+ FE9C              ;	x = ABS x: y =	ABS y
  45+ FE9C              ;
  46+ FE9C              ;	if x	>= y
  47+ FE9C              ;		if x+y=0 then return
  48+ FE9C              ;		H = x
  49+ FE9C              ;		L = y
  50+ FE9C              ;		ddx = direc_x
  51+ FE9C              ;		ddy = 0
  52+ FE9C              ;	else
  53+ FE9C              ;		H = y
  54+ FE9C              ;		L = x
  55+ FE9C              ;		ddx = 0
  56+ FE9C              ;		ddy = direc_y
  57+ FE9C              ;	endif
  58+ FE9C              ;
  59+ FE9C              ;	B = H
  60+ FE9C              ;	i = INT(B/2)
  61+ FE9C              ;	FOR N=B TO 1 STEP -1
  62+ FE9C              ;		i = i + L
  63+ FE9C              ;		if i	< H
  64+ FE9C              ;			ix =	ddx
  65+ FE9C              ;			iy =	ddy
  66+ FE9C              ;		else
  67+ FE9C              ;			i = i - H
  68+ FE9C              ;			ix =	direc_x
  69+ FE9C              ;			iy =	direc_y
  70+ FE9C              ;		endif
  71+ FE9C              ;		x0 =	x0 +	ix
  72+ FE9C              ;		y0 =	y0 +	iy
  73+ FE9C              ;		plot	(x0,y0)
  74+ FE9C              ;	NEXT	N
  75+ FE9C              ;
  76+ FE9C              ;
  77+ FE9C              ;	Registers	changed after return:
  78+ FE9C              ;		..BCDEHL/IXIY/af......	same
  79+ FE9C              ;		AF....../..../..bcdehl	different
  80+ FE9C              ;
  81+ FE9C 00 00        line_gfx_coords         dw  0
  82+ FE9E
  83+ FE9E              LineHLtoDE:
  84+ FE9E 7C           TestMaxY:               ld	a,h ; were h = y or l = y?
  85+ FE9F FE C0                                cp	192
  86+ FEA1 30 26                                jr	nc, exit_line		; y0	coordinate out	of range
  87+ FEA3 7A                                   ld	a,d
  88+ FEA4 FE C0                                cp	192
  89+ FEA6 30 21                                jr	nc, exit_line		; y1	coordinate out	of range
  90+ FEA8 22 9C FE                             ld	(line_gfx_coords),hl		; the starting	point is now default
  91+ FEAB E5                                   push	hl
  92+ FEAC D5                                   push	de
  93+ FEAD 6C                                   ld	l,h				; L = x0
  94+ FEAE 62                                   ld	h,d				; H = x1
  95+ FEAF 7C           distanceX:		        ld	a,h
  96+ FEB0 95                                   sub	l
  97+ FEB1 6F                                   ld	l,a
  98+ FEB2 26 00                                ld	h,0
  99+ FEB4 30 02                                jr	nc, distanceXDone
 100+ FEB6 26 FF                                ld	h,-1
 101+ FEB8 D1           distanceXDone:          pop	de
 102+ FEB9 E3                                   ex	(sp),hl			; L = y0
 103+ FEBA 63                                   ld	h,e				; H = y1
 104+ FEBB 7C           distanceY:		        ld	a,h
 105+ FEBC 95                                   sub	l
 106+ FEBD 6F                                   ld	l,a
 107+ FEBE 26 00                                ld	h,0
 108+ FEC0 30 02                                jr	nc, distanceYDone

 117+ FECA              ;	IN:	HL =	move	relative x horisontal points (maximum +/- 255).
 118+ FECA              ;		DE =	move	relative y vertical	points (maximum +/-	255).
 119+ FECA              ;
 120+ FECA              ; OUT: h - l distance in	HL

 129+ FED2 CD 52 FF                             call	absValue

 131+ FED6 E1           DrawLineGetVertRelative:pop	hl					; get relative	vertical movement
 132+ FED7 CD 45 FF                             call	sgn

 134+ FEDB CD 52 FF                             call	absValue

 207+ E0BC              ; Creates a 32x32 sprite based on first sprite number and pattern, then goes:
 208+ E0BC              ;    Spr,   pattern     spr+1, pattern+1
 209+ E0BC              ;    Spr+1, pattern+2   spr+3, pattern+3
 210+ E0BC              ; " sprite_big BC = row, hl= col D = sprite nbr , E= , pattern"
 211+ E0BC              ; note, BC and HL must be in correct range else they will mess up other byte's attributes, not masked for speed
 212+ E0BC              ; note this is based on full screen sprites including writing to border
 213+ E0BC              ; Currently can not get realtive sprites to work so will brute force it.
 214+ E0BC 7B           sprite_4x4:                 ld      a,e                                                         ; prep upper 2 bits as we will
 215+ E0BD F6 C0                                    or      %11000000                                                   ; Enable visible and 5th byte
 216+ E0BF 5F                                       ld      e,a                                                         ; a now holds value to use for anchor
 217+ E0C0                                          ;break

 220+ E0C8 79                                       ld      a,c

 222+ E0D0 7B                                       ld      a,e
 222+ E0D1 ED 92 38       nextreg   SPRITE_PORT_ATTR3_REGISTER,a        ; visible 5 bytes pattern e
 223+ E0D4 78                                       ld      a,b                                 ; get down MSB from b
 224+ E0D5 F6 20                                    or      %00100000
 224+ E0D7 ED 92 79       nextreg   SPRITE_PORT_MIRROR_ATTRIBUTE_4_WITH_INC,a       ; its going to be a unified "Big sprite" to uses rotations & scaling from anchor
 225+ E0DA              ;-- now process unified sprites
 226+ E0DA              .TopRightRelative:         ; inc     d
 227+ E0DA                                         ; ld      a,d         : nextreg  SPRITE_PORT_INDEX_REGISTER,a        ; set up sprite id + 1

 152++C0B9              ; UBnkaiatkecm
 153++C0B9              ; Bit	                Description
 154++C0B9              ; 7 -                   AI Enabled Flag
 155++C0B9              ; 6 -                   Ship Visible = ShipOnScreen/NotCloaked (cleared or set by check visible or cloaking override)
 156++C0B9              ; 5 -                   Ship is exploding if set, note if its a missile and one already equeued this will have to linger
 157++C0B9              ;                       linger can be done by not erasing ship unit missile equeue handled
 158++C0B9              ; 4 -                   Ship marked as exploded, cleared once aknowledged then bit 5 takes over and UBnKCloudCounter
 159++C0B9              ; 3 -                   Display state - Plot as a Dot
 160++C0B9              ; 2 -                   Nbr of Missiles bit 2
 161++C0B9              ; 1 -                   Nbr of Missiles bit 1
 162++C0B9              ; 0 -                   ECM present flag
 163++C0B9              ; ShipNewBitsAddr (in blueprint)
 164++C0B9              ;Bit	                Description
 165++C0B9              ;#0	Trader flag         * 0 = not a trader  * 1 = trader
 166++C0B9              ;                       80% of traders are peaceful and mind their own business plying their trade between the planet and space station, but 20% of them moonlight as bounty hunters (see bit #1)
 167++C0B9              ;                       Ships that are traders: Escape pod, Shuttle, Transporter, Anaconda, Rock hermit, Worm
 168++C0B9              ;#1 Bounty hunter flag  * 0 = not a bounty hunter* 1 = bounty hunter
 169++C0B9              ;                       If we are a fugitive or a serious offender and we bump into a bounty hunter, they will become hostile and attack us (see bit #2)
 170++C0B9              ;                       Ships that are bounty hunters: Viper, Fer-de-lance
 171++C0B9              ;#2	Hostile flag        * 0 = not hostile  * 1 = hostile
 172++C0B9              ;                       Hostile ships will attack us on sight; there are quite a few of them
 173++C0B9              ;                       Ships that are hostile: Sidewinder, Mamba, Krait, Adder, Gecko, Cobra Mk I, Worm, Cobra Mk III, Asp Mk II, Python (pirate), Moray, Thargoid, Thargon, Constrictor
 174++C0B9              ;#3	Pirate flag         * 0 = not a pirate * 1 = pirate
 175++C0B9              ;                       Hostile pirates will attack us on sight, but once we get inside the space station safe zone, they will stop
 176++C0B9              ;                       Ships that are pirates: Sidewinder, Mamba, Krait, Adder, Gecko, Cobra Mk I, Cobra Mk III, Asp Mk II, Python (pirate), Moray, Thargoid
 177++C0B9              ;#4	Docking flag        * 0 = not docking * 1 = docking
 178++C0B9              ;                       Traders with their docking flag set fly towards the space station to try to dock, otherwise they aim for the planet
 179++C0B9              ;                       This flag is randomly set for traders when they are spawned
 180++C0B9              ;                       Ships that can be docking: Escape pod, Shuttle, Transporter, Anaconda, Rock hermit, Worm
 181++C0B9              ;#5	Innocent bystander  * 0 = normal * 1 = innocent bystander
 182++C0B9              ;                       If we attack an innocent ship within the space station safe zone, then the station will get angry with us and start spawning cops
 183++C0B9              ;                       Ships that are innocent bystanders: Shuttle, Transporter, Cobra Mk III, Python, Boa, Anaconda, Rock hermit, Cougar
 184++C0B9              ;#6	Cop flag            * 0 = not a cop * 1 = cop
 185++C0B9              ;                       If we destroy a cop, then we instantly become a fugitive (the Transporter isn't actually a cop, but it's clearly under police protection)
 186++C0B9              ;                       Ships that are cops: Viper, Transporter
 187++C0B9              ;#7	Scooped, docked, escape pod flag
 188++C0B9              ;                       For spawned ships, this flag indicates that the ship been scooped or has docked (bit 7 is always clear on spawning)
 189++C0B9              ;                       For blueprints, this flag indicates whether the ship type has an escape pod fitted, so it can launch it when in dire straits
 190++C0B9              ;                       Ships that have escape pods: Cobra Mk III, Python, Boa, Anaconda, Rock hermit, Viper, Mamba, Krait, Adder, Cobra Mk I, Cobra Mk III (pirate), Asp Mk II, Python (pirate), Fer-de-lance

1477+ D757              ; Pitch and roll are 2 phases
1478+ D757              ; 1 - we apply our pitch and roll to the ship position
1479+ D757              ;       x -> x + alpha * (y - alpha * x)
1480+ D757              ;       y -> y - alpha * x - beta * z
1481+ D757              ;       z -> z + beta * (y - alpha * x - beta * z)
1482+ D757              ; which can be simplified as:
1483+ D757              ;       1. K2 = y - alpha * x
1484+ D757              ;       2. z = z + beta * K2
1485+ D757              ;       3. y = K2 - beta * z
1486+ D757              ;       4. x = x + alpha * y
1487+ D757              ; 2 - we apply our patch and roll to the ship orientation
1488+ D757              ;      Roll calculations:
1489+ D757              ;
1490+ D757              ;        nosev_y = nosev_y - alpha * nosev_x_hi
1491+ D757              ;        nosev_x = nosev_x + alpha * nosev_y_hi
1492+ D757              ;      Pitch calculations:
1493+ D757              ;
1494+ D757              ;        nosev_y = nosev_y - beta * nosev_z_hi
1495+ D757              ;        nosev_z = nosev_z + beta * nosev_y_hi
1496+ D757
1497+ D757
1498+ D757              ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 559+ C4EC              ; Pitch and roll are 2 phases
 560+ C4EC              ; 1 - we apply our pitch and roll to the ship position
 561+ C4EC              ;       x -> x + alpha * (y - alpha * x)
 562+ C4EC              ;       y -> y - alpha * x - beta * z
 563+ C4EC              ;       z -> z + beta * (y - alpha * x - beta * z)
 564+ C4EC              ; which can be simplified as:
 565+ C4EC              ;       1. K2 = y - alpha * x
 566+ C4EC              ;       2. z = z + beta * K2
 567+ C4EC              ;       3. y = K2 - beta * z
 568+ C4EC              ;       4. x = x + alpha * y
 569+ C4EC              ; 2 - we apply our patch and roll to the ship orientation
 570+ C4EC              ;      Roll calculations:
 571+ C4EC              ;
 572+ C4EC              ;        nosev_y = nosev_y - alpha * nosev_x_hi
 573+ C4EC              ;        nosev_x = nosev_x + alpha * nosev_y_hi
 574+ C4EC              ;      Pitch calculations:
 575+ C4EC              ;
 576+ C4EC              ;        nosev_y = nosev_y - beta * nosev_z_hi
 577+ C4EC              ;        nosev_z = nosev_z + beta * nosev_y_hi

  14++C4EC              ;  4. x = x + alpha * y
  15++C4EC              ;.... or
  16++C4EC              ;  2. z = z + (beta * (y - alpha * x))
  17++C4EC              ;  3. y = (y - alpha * x) - (beta * z)
  18++C4EC              ;  4. x = x + (alpha * y)
  19++C4EC
  20++C4EC
  21++C4EC              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  22++C4EC              ; Sun version of pitch and roll is a 24 bit calculation 1 bit sign + 23 bit value
  23++C4EC              ; Need to write a test routine for roll and pitchs
  24++C4EC              ; Minsky Roll       Minsky Pitch
  25++C4EC              ;  y -= alpha * x    y -= beta * z
  26++C4EC              ;  x += alpha * y    z += beta * y
  27++C4EC              ; or once combined
  28++C4EC              ;   1. K2 = y - alpha * x
  29++C4EC              ;   2. z = z + beta * K2
  30++C4EC              ;   3. y = K2 - beta * z
  31++C4EC              ;   4. x = x + alpha * y
  32++C4EC              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  33++C4EC              ;	alpha = flight_roll / 256.0;
  34++C4EC              ;	beta = flight_climb / 256.0;
  35++C4EC              ;    k2 = y - alpha * x;
  36++C4EC              ;	z = z + beta * k2;
  37++C4EC              ;	y = k2 - z * beta;
  38++C4EC              ;	x = x + alpha * y;
  39++C4EC              ;divs32   dehl = dehl' / dehl in our case it will be S78.0/ 0S78.0 to give us 0S78.0
  40++C4EC              ; Performs minsky rotation based on play. As sun is a ball no local rotation is needed
  41++C4EC DD 21 10 C0  SunApplyMyRollAndPitch:     ld      ix,SBnKxlo                  ; base location of position as 24 bit
  42++C4F0                                          MMUSelectMathsBankedFns
  42++C4F0 ED 91 50 66 >                     nextreg MathsBankedFnsMMU, BankMathsBankedFns
  43++C4F4 CD B4 08                                 call    ApplyMyRollAndPitchIX
  44++C4F7 CD 3F 0A                                 call    Normalise24IX
  45++C4FA CD 20 0A                                 call    UpdateCompassIX
  46++C4FD C9           							ret

 103+ C12B                                          ClippingCodeLL28Macro P
 103+ C12B 21 38 F1    >P_LL28_6502:         ld      hl,Qvar                 ; CMP Q                  \ If A >= Q, then the answer will not fit in one byte,
 103+ C12E 4E          >                            ld      c,(hl)                  ; using c as Q var
 103+ C12F B9          >                            cp      c
 103+ C130             >                            FlipCarryFlag
 103+ C130 3F          >                        ccf
 103+ C131 DA 59 C1    >                            jp      c, P_LL2_6502    ; BCS LL2                \ so jump to LL2 to return 255
 103+ C134 06 FE       >                            ld      b,$FE                   ; LDX #%11111110         \ Set R to have bits 1-7 set, so we can rotate through 7 loop iterations, getting a 1 each time, and then we use b as Rvar
 103+ C136 CB 27       >P_LL31_6502:          sla     a                       ; ASL A                  \ Shift A to the left
 103+ C138 DA 4D C1    >                            jp      c, P_LL29_6502             ; BCS LL29               \ If bit 7 of A was set, then jump straight to the subtraction
 103+ C13B             >                            FlipCarryFlag                   ;                          If A < N, then C flag is set.
 103+ C13B 3F          >                        ccf
 103+ C13C             >                            JumpIfALTNusng c, P_LL31_SKIPSUB_6502 ; CMP Q              \ If A < Q, skip the following subtraction
 103+ C13C B9          >                        cp      c
 103+ C13D DA 42 C1    >                        jp		c, P_LL31_SKIPSUB_6502
 103+ C140             >                                                                ; BCC P%+4
 103+ C140 91          >                            sub     c                       ; SBC Q                  \ A >= Q, so set A = A - Q
 103+ C141             >                            ClearCarryFlag
 103+ C141 B7          >                        or a
 103+ C142             >P_LL31_SKIPSUB_6502:  FlipCarryFlag
 103+ C142 3F          >                        ccf
 103+ C143 CB 10       >                            rl      b                       ; ROL R                  \ Rotate the counter in R to the left, and catch the result bit into bit 0 (which will be a 0 if we didn't do the subtraction, or 1 if we did)
 103+ C145 DA 36 C1    >                            jp      c, P_LL31_6502            ; BCS LL31               \ If we still have set bits in R, loop back to LL31 to do the next iteration of 7
 103+ C148 78          >                            ld      a,b
 103+ C149 32 39 F1    >                            ld      (Rvar),a
 103+ C14C C9          >                            ret                             ; RTS                    \ R left with remainder of division
 103+ C14D 91          >P_LL29_6502:          sub     c                       ; SBC Q                  \ A >= Q, so set A = A - Q
 103+ C14E             >                            SetCarryFlag                    ; SEC                    \ Set the C flag to rotate into the result in R
 103+ C14E 37          >                        scf
 103+ C14F CB 10       >                            rl      b                       ; ROL R                  \ Rotate the counter in R to the left, and catch the result bit into bit 0 (which will be a 0 if we didn't do the subtraction, or 1 if we did)
 103+ C151 DA 36 C1    >                            jp      c, P_LL31_6502            ; BCS LL31               \ If we still have set bits in R, loop back to LL31 to do the next iteration of 7
 103+ C154 78          >                            ld      a,b                     ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine with R containing the
 103+ C155 32 39 F1    >                            ld      (Rvar),a                ; .

 339+ E103 DD 21 37 E0  scan_keyboard:          ld		ix,RawKeys                      ; hl = table of raw IO port readings
 340+ E107 21 41 E0                             ld		hl,KeyAddrTab                   ; de = table of IO ports to read
 341+ E10A 0E 08                                ld		c,8                             ; 8 ports to ready
 342+ E10C 11 00 E0                             ld      de,Keys                         ; ix = table of key states from raw read
 343+ E10F 7E           .PortReadLoop:          ld		a,(hl)							; Set up port to read as (hl)$FE
 344+ E110 DB FE                                in		a,($FE)							; read port to a
 345+ E112 DD 77 00                             ld      (ix+0),a                        ; save raw scan
 346+ E115 DD 23                                inc     ix
 347+ E117 23                                   inc		hl                              ; and ready for next read

 370+ 0896 3F          >                        ccf

 372+ 0899 DA 8A 08                             jp      c, .LL31_6502           ; BCS LL31               \ If we still have set bits in R, loop back to LL31 to do the next iteration of 7
 373+ 089C 78                                   ld      a,b
 374+ 089D 32 F0 7F                             ld      (varR),a
 375+ 08A0 C9                                   ret                             ; RTS                    \ R left with remainder of division
 376+ 08A1 91           .LL29_6502:             sub     c                       ; SBC Q                  \ A >= Q, so set A = A - Q
 377+ 08A2                                      SetCarryFlag                    ; SEC                    \ Set the C flag to rotate into the result in R
 377+ 08A2 37          >                        scf
 378+ 08A3 CB 10                                rl      b                       ; ROL R                  \ Rotate the counter in R to the left, and catch the result bit into bit 0 (which will be a 0 if we didn't do the subtraction, or 1 if we did)
 379+ 08A5 DA 8A 08                             jp      c, .LL31_6502           ; BCS LL31               \ If we still have set bits in R, loop back to LL31 to do the next iteration of 7
 380+ 08A8 78                                   ld      a,b                     ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine with R containing the
 381+ 08A9 32 F0 7F                             ld      (varR),a                ; .
 382+ 08AC C9                                   ret                             ; .                      \ remainder of the division
 383+ 08AD 3E FF        .LL2_6502:              ld      a,$FF                   ; LDA #255               \ The division is very close to 1, so return the closest
 384+ 08AF 32 F0 7F                             ld      (varR),a                ; STA R                  \ possible answer to 256, i.e. R = 255
 385+ 08B2                                      SetCarryFlag                    ; we failed so need carry flag set
 385+ 08B2 37          >                        scf
 386+ 08B3 C9                                   ret                             ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine

   1+ 0A0C              ; Updates compass based on vertex positions in IX
   2+ 0A0C              ; IX structure is3 x 24 bit (x, y, z) followed by two 16t bit Compass X, Y
   3+ 0A0C              ; compas range is +-14 so we scale to +-16 and if result (or result + 1) has bit 5 set then clamp to 14 +-
   4+ 0A0C              ; Compass position is based on the normals for position relative to player scaled to +/- 16
   5+ 0A0C
   6+ 0A0C              ; For Normal to compass we take the leading sign Normal in BC as the basis
   7+ 0A0C              ; as its not 2's compliment. The result is a
   8+ 0A0C
   9+ 0A0C              ; When written to compass position its a 2's compliment +/- 15
  10+ 0A0C              ; Takes bc = Normal and returns HL with 2's compliment offset +/-15
  11+ 0A0C
  12+ 0A0C 79           NormalToCompassSigned:  ld      a,c
  13+ 0A0D ED 23                                swapnib
  14+ 0A0F E6 0F                                and     $0F
  15+ 0A11 CB 78                                bit     7,b
  16+ 0A13 C2 1A 0A                             jp      nz,.NormalNegative
  17+ 0A16 26 00        .NormalPositive:        ld      h,0
  18+ 0A18 6F                                   ld      l,a
  19+ 0A19 C9                                   ret
  20+ 0A1A ED 44        .NormalNegative:        neg
  21+ 0A1C 26 FF                                ld      h,$FF
  22+ 0A1E 6F                                   ld      l,a
  23+ 0A1F C9                                   ret

   2+ 0A3F              ; takes a 3x24 bit vector and normalilses them, this is done by taking the ABS values scaling down into a maxioum of a 15 bit number
   3+ 0A3F
   4+ 0A3F              PrepScale:              MACRO                       ;setg [A IYH] to or'ed all bytes of ABS X,Y,Z
   5+ 0A3F ~                                    ld      a,h
   6+ 0A3F ~                                    or      d
   7+ 0A3F ~                                    or      c
   8+ 0A3F ~                                    ld      iyh,a
   9+ 0A3F ~                                    ld      a,l

  40+ 0A3F              CalculateScale:         MACRO
  41+ 0A3F ~                                    ld      iyl,a

  43+ 0A3F ~                                    ld      b,0
  44+ 0A3F ~                                    ld      de,iy               ; moving iy to de for faster bit and shift operations

  46+ 0A3F ~            .ScaleLoop:             bit     6,d                 ; this loop will find the minium number of shifts requried

   1+ 0DCB              ; fast 16-bit isqrt by Zeda Thomas
   2+ 0DCB              ;Feel free to use for whatever :)
   3+ 0DCB
   4+ 0DCB              sqrtHL:
   5+ 0DCB              ;Input: HL
   6+ 0DCB              ;Output: A is the integer square root of HL
   7+ 0DCB              ;Destroys: HL,DE (D is actually 0)
   8+ 0DCB              ;min: 343cc
   9+ 0DCB              ;max: 380cc
  10+ 0DCB              ;avg: 361.5cc
  11+ 0DCB              ;88 bytes
  12+ 0DCB 11 40 50                             ld de,05040h                ; 10
  13+ 0DCE 7C                                   ld a,h                      ; 4
  14+ 0DCF 93                                   sub e                       ; 4
  15+ 0DD0 30 03                                jr nc,sq7                   ;\
  16+ 0DD2 83                                   add a,e                     ; | branch 1: 12cc
  17+ 0DD3 16 10                                ld d,16                     ; | branch 2: 18cc
  18+ 0DD5 BA           sq7:                    cp d                        ; 4
  19+ 0DD6 38 03                                jr c,sq6                    ;\
  20+ 0DD8 92                                   sub d                       ; | branch 1: 12cc
  21+ 0DD9 CB EA                                set 5,d                     ; | branch 2: 19cc
  22+ 0DDB CB A2        sq6:                    res 4,d                     ; 8
  23+ 0DDD CB 3A                                srl d                       ; 8
  24+ 0DDF CB D2                                set 2,d                     ; 8
  25+ 0DE1 BA                                   cp d                        ; 4
  26+ 0DE2 38 03                                jr c,sq5                    ;\
  27+ 0DE4 92                                   sub d                       ; | branch 1: 12cc
  28+ 0DE5 CB DA                                set 3,d                     ; | branch 2: 19cc
  29+ 0DE7 CB 3A        sq5:                    srl d                       ; 8
  30+ 0DE9 3C                                   inc a                       ; 4
  31+ 0DEA 92                                   sub d                       ; 4
  32+ 0DEB 30 03                                jr nc,sq4                   ;\
  33+ 0DED 15                                   dec d                       ; | branch 1: 12cc
  34+ 0DEE 82                                   add a,d                     ; | branch 2: 19cc
  35+ 0DEF 15                                   dec d                       ; | <-- this resets the low bit of D, so `srl d` resets carry.
  36+ 0DF0 CB 3A        sq4:                     srl d                      ; 8
  37+ 0DF2 67                                   ld h,a                      ; 4
  38+ 0DF3 7B                                   ld a,e                      ; 4
  39+ 0DF4 ED 52                                sbc hl,de                   ; 15
  40+ 0DF6 30 01                                jr nc,sq3                   ;\
  41+ 0DF8 19                                   add hl,de                   ; | 12cc or 18cc
  42+ 0DF9 3F           sq3:                    ccf                         ; 4

  44+ 0DFB CB 3A                                srl d                       ; 8
  45+ 0DFD 1F                                   rra                         ; 4
  46+ 0DFE 5F                                   ld e,a                      ; 4
